title: perf-bench-scratch-avery-li-2026-03-28
content:
Perf bench scratchpad - Avery Li (notes + quick runs)

Context / goal:
- Re-run quick latency/throughput matrix for model variants (fp16 vs 8-bit quantized) to validate perf delta on A100 and H100.
- Focus: single-request p50/p95 latency for short (32 tok) and long (512 tok) sequences, plus steady-state throughput with batching.
- Check KV cache impact for chat-style prefix reuse.

Hardware + infra:
- A100 80GB (nc1) and H100 80GB (nc2) instances in us-west.
- Serving runtime: local dev branch feat/batching-opt (commit abc123).
- Runner: python perf_runner.py (args below) inside container image: ghcr.io/redwood-inference/perf:2026-03-25

Commands used (simplified):
- base: python perf_runner.py --model gpt-open-v2 --dtype fp16 --gpu A100 --seq_len 32 --batch 1 --iters 200
- quant: python perf_runner.py --model gpt-open-v2-8bit --dtype int8 --gpu A100 --seq_len 32 --batch 1 --iters 200
- kv: python perf_runner.py --model chat-gpt-open-v2 --kv_cache true --prefix_len 128 --seq_len 32 --batch 1 --iters 200
- throughput sweep: python perf_runner.py --model gpt-open-v2 --dtype fp16 --gpu H100 --seq_len 512 --batch_sizes "[1,2,4,8,16,32]" --steady true --duration 180

Raw results (selected) - A100:
- fp16, seq32, batch1: p50 18.3 ms, p95 34.5 ms, mean 20.1 ms (200 iters)
- int8, seq32, batch1: p50 16.1 ms, p95 30.7 ms, mean 17.6 ms (200 iters)
- fp16, seq512, batch1: p50 210 ms, p95 330 ms, mean 225 ms (50 iters)
- kv enabled (prefix 128) seq32: p50 10.2 ms, p95 18.9 ms (cache hit for continuation tokens)

Raw results (selected) - H100:
- fp16, seq32, batch1: p50 12.8 ms, p95 22.1 ms, mean 13.7 ms
- int8, seq32, batch1: p50 11.6 ms, p95 20.3 ms, mean 12.4 ms
- fp16, seq512, batch1: p50 140 ms, p95 210 ms
- throughput sweep (seq512): batch1 360 tok/s, batch2 680 tok/s, batch4 1240 tok/s, batch8 2200 tok/s, batch16 2800 tok/s, batch32 2900 tok/s (diminishing returns after 16)

Observations / quick conclusions:
- H100 shows ~30-40% lower latency than A100 for same fp16 runs, consistent with expectations.
- 8-bit quant gives ~10-15% latency improvement on both GPUs for short sequences; effect smaller on long sequences (kernel overhead + dequant).
- KV cache delivers big p50 improvements for chat-style continuation (approx 40-50% reduction) but depends on prefix size and cache miss penalty.
- Batching increases throughput substantially up to batch 16 on H100 for seq512. After batch 16 we hit memory / kernel scheduling limits and marginal gains.
- p95 tails are sensitive to garbage collection spikes in the container; need better isolation or pinned CPU cores for the runner.

Notes on methodology caveats:
- These are single-run quick experiments (not multiple seeds). Will need 3-run averages for release-grade numbers.
- Workload tokenization: using tokenizer v2.1.1 (subword). Make sure to normalize input length when comparing.
- Network overhead: tests were local to the instance to minimize RDMA/ethernet variance. Not identical to Hosted API environment.

Next steps / todo:
- [ ] Repeat key points (fp16 vs int8) with 3 runs each and collect stddev for p50/p95.
- [ ] Run on larger fleet (2x A100 nodes) to validate distributed KV cache hit rates and cross-GPU batching behavior.
- [ ] Add profiling trace (triton/cupti) for one long seq512 run to identify kernel stalls causing p95 spikes.
- [ ] Try fed batch scheduling tweak from feat/batching-opt and compare latency/throughput.
- [ ] Open GH issue to track container GC/p95 problem (link to perf repo).

Quick hypotheses to test:
- Hypothesis 1: int8 quant will have minimal impact on p95 for long sequences due to dequant overhead per attention block. Test by instrumenting kernel time per layer.
- Hypothesis 2: p95 spikes correlate with host CPU throttling from other co-located tasks (pin runner to isolated CPU set).

References / links (local):
- run logs: /mnt/perf_runs/2026-03-28/avery-a100-fp16.log
- perf scripts: https://github.com/redwood-inference/bench-scripts/blob/main/perf_runner.py
- previous notes: perf-bench-scratch-jordan-lee-2026-03-07 (see Drive)

Scratch calculations (throughput -> tok/s approximations):
- H100 batch8 seq512: observed 2200 tok/s roughly -> per-request throughput per GPU approx 2200/8 = 275 tok/s per request
- Memory headroom estimate: batch16 at seq512 uses ~72GB on H100 image (close to limit)

Questions / unresolved:
- What's the target p95 SLA for hosted customers on 1 token continuation? Ops says target p95 < 50ms for short seqs on Hosted S-tier. Need to confirm exact SLO per plan.
- Should we prefer int8 by default for short-seq chat workloads? Need quality regression eval on representative prompts.

Log snippets (examples):
- 2026-03-28 14:12:03 INFO request=12345 model=gpt-open-v2 dtype=fp16 seq=32 latency_ms=18.7
- 2026-03-28 14:12:34 WARN mem=72GB batch=16 kernel=cuBlas timeout=0.02

If I'm OOO next week: Jordan please run 3x repeats for A100 fp16 vs int8 (seq32 + seq512) and drop CSVs into /mnt/perf_runs/2026-03-31/ for aggregation.
